prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (2010)

- Taxes and revenues
  - Raise the personal income tax allowance to £10,000, removing 3.6m low earners from income tax and cutting most taxpayers’ bills by about £700.
  - Funded by: equalising capital gains tax with income tax rates; restricting pension tax relief to the basic rate; a 1% annual levy on residential property value above £2m; anti-avoidance measures; replacing Air Passenger Duty with a per-plane duty, including a higher rate for domestic flights with viable alternatives.

- Public finances
  - Begin deficit reduction from 2011–12, with an emergency budget and a cross-party financial stability council.
  - Identified savings include: scrapping ID cards, biometric passports, ContactPoint, and the Intercept Modernisation Programme; a £400 cap on annual public sector pay rises for two years; reforming tax credits and winter fuel payments; ending Child Trust Fund contributions; a banking levy; cutting central government bureaucracy and inspections; reforming prisons (presumption against sentences under 6 months); cancelling Eurofighter Tranche 3B; reducing MoD administration/top ranks; scaling back RDAs; cutting consultancy and civil service bonuses; and “stop” low-priority projects.

- Economy, banking, jobs
  - Separate retail and investment banking; banking levy until separation complete; reform bonuses; expand local and regional finance (Local Enterprise Funds, Regional Stock Exchanges); get state-influenced banks lending to viable firms.
  - One-year job-creation/green stimulus (c.100,000 jobs): shipyard upgrades for offshore renewables, eco cash-back for home upgrades, energy-efficiency loans for public buildings, bringing 250k empty homes into use, bus scrappage.
  - Establish a UK Infrastructure Bank to mobilise private capital for transport and energy networks.

- Business, innovation, work
  - Reduce red tape (sunset clauses, “one in, one out”), end “gold-plating” of EU rules, move business rates to site value and local control, restore a public interest test for takeovers, support superfast broadband, use procurement to grow green markets.
  - Support mutuals/co-ops; restructure Royal Mail (49% sale; employee/government ownership split) and keep Post Office in public ownership; convert Northern Rock to a building society.
  - Protect science funding baselines; peer-review decisions; open access to state-funded research; maintain adviser independence.
  - Workplace: extend flexible working to all; name-blind recruitment and pay audits for firms >100 staff; publish high pay (>£200k) in public companies; improve disability employment support.

- Education and skills
  - £2.5bn “pupil premium” targeted at disadvantaged pupils; smaller classes; more one-to-one tuition; early SEN assessment; stronger teacher recruitment/training; anti-bullying.
  - Create an independent standards authority; slim curriculum; scale back primary testing; unify academic/vocational routes via a General Diploma; allow 14–19 study at colleges; reform league tables.
  - School autonomy via local commissioning; inclusive admissions in faith schools; more flexible pay structures.
  - Phase out undergraduate tuition fees over six years (final-year fees scrapped immediately); national bursary scheme; more Foundation Degrees and adult apprenticeships; retarget adult skills funding.

- Health and care
  - Shift resources from central bureaucracy to frontline services; halve the Department of Health; abolish Strategic Health Authorities; integrate health and social care; expand mental health therapies; prioritise dementia research; targeted alcohol measures; reduce air pollution.
  - Patient entitlements for timely diagnosis/treatment; elected Local Health Boards; GP choice and email access; staff budget control; safety transparency; language/competence checks for doctors.

- Families, older people, consumers
  - Shared parental leave; antenatal time-off for fathers; flexible working for all; youth services statutory; minimum wage parity >16 (except apprentices); default shared parenting presumption where safe.
  - Restore earnings link for the state pension with a 2.5% floor; end compulsory retirement ages; more respite support for carers; more flexible pension access/annuitisation.
  - Consumer measures: fairer energy tariffs and social tariffs; water charge reforms; cap unfair bank/transaction fees; PostBank; cap credit/store card interest; rail fare reductions; airline pricing transparency; regulate private clamping.

- Climate, environment, transport
  - Net zero-carbon by 2050; at least −40% emissions by 2020; 40% of electricity from non-carbon sources by 2020 (rising to 100% by 2050); offshore/marine priority; renewable heat; European supergrid; reject new nuclear; no unabated coal; 30% energy-efficiency target by 2020; decade-long home retrofit offer.
  - Aviation: per-plane duty; higher domestic rate where alternatives exist; cancel Heathrow third runway and other South East expansions.
  - Transport: shift funds from major roads to local rail; cut regulated rail fares; reform Network Rail; empower councils on buses; promote cycling/walking; prepare revenue-neutral road pricing in a second parliament; rural fuel discount.
  - Countryside/housing: expand access; restore local planning control and third-party appeals; zero-waste targets; biodiversity recovery by 2020; equalise VAT on repair/new build; protect greenfield and gardens; double woodland by 2050; restrict building in floodplains; smart meters in shortage areas; bring empty homes into use; energy-efficient new builds; enable council housebuilding.

- International, defence and development
  - EU: stronger financial regulation, CAP reform, budget efficiency; maintain justice tools with safeguards; in/out referendum upon any fundamental treaty change.
  - Defence: strategic review; cancel Eurofighter Tranche 3B; no like-for-like Trident replacement; increase lower-rank pay; accelerate service housing upgrades; reduce MoD overheads; enhance European cooperation.
  - Foreign policy: EU diplomatic weight; conditions-based Afghanistan strategy; arms trade controls; investigate torture/rendition allegations; two-state approach in the Middle East; diplomacy/sanctions on Iran.
  - Development: 0.7% GNI on aid by 2013 in law; new finance (e.g., FTT; aviation/shipping carbon markets); curb tax havens/corrupt flows; focus on health, education, water, gender; debt relief; climate adaptation funding additional to aid.

- Policing, justice, immigration
  - 3,000 more police with less paperwork and elected police authorities; evidence-led crime reduction; share anonymised hospital data to target violence; better hate crime recording; drug policy based on independent science; treatment-focused approach for users.
  - Expand restorative justice; neighbourhood panels; end short custodial sentences presumption.
  - Borders: reintroduce exit checks; create a National Border Force; regional points-based work system; tougher employer enforcement; prioritise deporting serious offenders; earned citizenship for long-resident, law-abiding, English-speaking undocumented migrants (pre-2010).
  - Asylum: independent agency; EU coordination; permit work; end child detention; alternatives to detention; no removals to danger.

- Political reform and civil liberties
  - Proportional voting for MPs; votes at 16; fixed-term parliaments; a fully elected second chamber with fewer members; stronger Commons scrutiny; written constitution via citizens’ convention and referendum; cap donations at £10k; recall for wrongdoing; lobbying transparency; domicile/residency requirements for parliamentarians/candidates.
  - Devolution: new powers for Scotland and Wales; needs-based funding formula; resolve specified Scottish revenue anomalies; review England’s status via constitutional convention.
  - Civil liberties: a Freedom Bill (CCTV regulation, limit council surveillance, fair extradition, jury trial protections, protest rights, libel reform); scrap ID cards and expanded biometric passports; halt expansive data retention; remove innocent DNA records; protect Human Rights Act; counterterrorism reforms (end control orders; 14-day pre-charge limit; allow intercept evidence; more post-charge questioning).
